author: nflaig
content:
the problem is that the current spec allows two griefing attacks
- (1) an IL committee member can release a IL after the deadline, right before the proposer picks the bid, which means no builder can satisfy the conditions. this could even be abused by a builder, they can produce a very low bid, that satisfies it, while all other bids don't, and if proposer enforces this rule, you can very cheaply win a slot
- (2) a builder can gossip a very high bid early into the previous slot (even before IL deadline) and which blocks all lower bids from propagating but the builder bid will not be picked by the proposer, essentially crowding out all other bids for free

author: jih2nn
content:
- Sounds valid. Should the spec just mention that a proposer should try their best to cover attesters' IL views?
- I don't follow (2).

author: nflaig
content:
- (1) yes that would solve it
- (2) a builder can just send a bid in the previous slot before the IL deadline with empty `inclusion_list_bits` and a very high bid value, due to `[IGNORE] This is the highest value bid seen for the slot and parent` nodes will ignore any further bids, but at selection time, the proposer will not pick the bid since it doesn't satisfy their view of ILs, so essentially a builder can outcrowd all other bids for free and force local build

author: jih2nn

Maybe I misread but it seems it's changed from very low bid to very high bid? Regardless, changing that part of the spec to let clients to do their best attempt to cover attesters' IL views will solve the issue.
